question: Contribution (i) claims one frozen checkpoint serves every backbone. The control that claim needs is the specialist: a module of the same architecture trained on one backbone only, evaluated on that backbone. If the shared module is not measurably worse, generality is free; if it is worse, we owe the reader the size of the toll.

base.reason: the control must be against the model we ship, not the 142-channel configuration the ablations were first registered against

backbones.applies_to: training clips and validation clips alike; the specialist selects its checkpoint on its own backbone's D2 validation, as a practitioner training for that backbone would

epochs.reason: matched optimisation budget. Twelve epochs over three backbones is thirty-six backbone-epochs of gradient steps; twelve epochs over one backbone would be a third of the budget, and a specialist that lost under that handicap would prove nothing.

everything_else_unchanged: clip length 4, batch size 4, AdamW, lr 2e-4, weight decay 1e-4, grad clip 1.0
coverage threshold 0.5, tau_reset 5.0 px native, tau_fusion 1.0 px native, alpha_reg 0.2
recurrent memory state, best-validation-EPE checkpoint selection

endpoint.primary: held-out D7 relative EPE and Bad1 reduction on the arm's own backbone cells, specialist against the shipped generalist checkpoint on those same cells
endpoint.protocol: the definitive evaluation used for Table I, restricted to one backbone; no new support, no new aggregation

declared_asymmetry: Every deviation above favours the specialist: matched gradient budget, three times as many selection points, and validation on its own backbone rather than a mean over three. The generalist gets none of that. This is deliberate -- a shared module that survives an advantaged specialist is the only version of the comparison worth reporting -- and it means a specialist win of ordinary size is not evidence against the shared module, while a specialist loss is.
reading_rule: The three-seed spread of the shipped head's D7 Bad1 reduction is 0.22 points and its registered threshold is 0.37. These arms are single-seed, so a difference below 0.37 points is not read at all, and a difference above it is read as a bound pending seeds, not as a measurement.

addendum_2026_08_27.added: DRENDS, out of domain, on the arm's own backbone, reported alongside D2 and D7
addendum_2026_08_27.reason: D7 is held-out sequences of the dataset the specialist trained on, which is the arena where a single-backbone module is strongest. Reporting the control only there would measure it where it is most favoured and skip the arena sharing exists to win -- arena selection, in a paper that spends a section naming selection optimism.
addendum_2026_08_27.status: reported, not promoted: the registered primary endpoint remains held-out D7 Bad1. DRENDS is an additional arena and is read as such.
addendum_2026_08_27.declared_before: any specialist evaluation had written a result to disk; the D2/D7 evaluation was running and results/specialist_eval was empty when this was written
addendum_2026_08_27.expected_direction: if the shared module's advantage is real it should be largest here, since a specialist trained on one backbone has the least diversity to generalise from. A specialist winning out of domain would be the strongest evidence against contribution (i) this control can produce.
